note: Findings listed here are reported in the sanitizer summary and do not fail a gating run.
Nothing here claims a defect is absent or harmless. It claims somebody owns it, and that
stopping every pull request on it buys nothing.
tool and kind must match exactly. where is matched as a substring against the finding's
sen:: frames and its source paths, and names a file rather than a line: lines move under
ordinary editing, and an entry that silently stops matching turns the gate red for a
finding this list was written to cover.
Every entry needs a reason and a removal condition. stale-when-gone is optional and names
a path whose disappearance a run can check for itself.

findings.reason: Seen once in roughly eight full suites, at remote_interest_manager.cpp:223, in code the concurrency redesign deletes whole. Registered in that redesign's ledger. Matched on the source path: no raw report survives, so the sen:: frame it groups under is not known here.
findings.remove-when: The redesign merges to main and remote_interest_manager.cpp leaves it; that merge drops this entry or records why not. Not an all-clear: the deleted site cannot recur, but the class -- a stored callable collected from a pool after its backing died -- is a design target of the replacement, not a certified absence.

findings.kind: member access within null pointer of type 'descriptor_state'
findings.reason: Upstream, at epoll_reactor.ipp:407 in asio 1.36.0: deregister_descriptor nulls the descriptor state under that object's own mutex, so a thread reaching start_op afterwards dereferences null. chriskohlhoff/asio#686 is open with no fix, so moving the pin does not help.
findings.remove-when: Upstream fixes it and conanfile.py requires a release carrying the fix.
